description: The serotonin and PDF roaming/dwelling circuit, as the cited sources support it. Neuron classes; left/right members are both gated.

sources: Flavell 2013 Fig 3A-B (NSM required; HSN also required, not modelled as a release site here)
Rhoades 2019 Fig 1-3 (NSM senses ingested food via DEL-3/DEL-7)

receptor.name: MOD-1
sources: Flavell 2013 Fig 3D-G (AIY+ASI+RID rescue together; RIF alone sufficient; ablating AIY, ASI or RIF reduces exploration)
receptor.conflict: Dag 2023 Fig 5G-I: in an acute-slowing assay, mod-1 rescue in RIF gives sustained slowing but rescue in AIY does not; a different behaviour from roaming/dwelling

sources: Flavell 2013 Fig 6E (Cre deletion of pdf-1 in AVB, PVP and SIAV removes rescue)

receptor.name: PDFR-1
sources: Flavell 2013 Fig 6G-H (partial rescue in AIY, RIM and RIA), Fig 7A-D (cAMP; adenylyl cyclase drives roaming)
receptor.excluded: RIB: Ji 2021 cites Rhoades 2019 for it, and Rhoades 2019 does not contain it

timescale_s.basis: NSM calcium peaks last about 60 s (Flavell 2013 Fig 4; Ji 2021 Fig 2); the circuit, not the concentration, is to carry persistence beyond it (Ji 2021, mutual inhibition)

mutant_directions.tph-1: more roaming (Flavell 2013 Fig 2C-D; Ji 2021 Fig 3A-B; Ji 2021 patch assay)
mutant_directions.pdfr-1: more dwelling (Flavell 2013 Fig 6A-C; Ji 2021 patch assay)

satiety: after 1 h starvation, worms on food roam about half as much (Ben Arous 2009 Fig 1); fasting increases NSM's response to food (Rhoades 2019 Fig 5)
verified: 2026-10-11, against the full texts: Flavell 2013 (PMC3942133), Ji 2021 (PMC8660023), Dag 2023 (PMC10484565), Rhoades 2019 (PMC6526957), Ben Arous 2009 (PMC2762077); figure images were not read, only text and legends
